q: When is my first I-983 evaluation due?
answer: Before the one-year anniversary of the start date of the STEM OPT employment authorization.

q: For the progress evaluation part of the I-983, what am I supposed to write about in my self-review?
answer: A self-evaluation of progress against the training plan's goals: accomplishments, knowledge and skills gained, and whether goals or skill areas need changing.

q: How many hours a week do I have to work at minimum on STEM OPT?
answer: 20 hours per week.

q: How quickly does my employer have to tell the DSO if I leave my job during STEM OPT?
answer: Within five business days of the termination or departure.

q: I'm a nonresident alien working in the US for a foreign company. Can my treaty country let me avoid US tax on my wages if I'm only here a short time?
answer: Yes, under many treaties with an income from employment article, you can exempt wages if you are present in the US for no more than 183 days in a 12-month period, the income is paid by a foreign employer, and the income is not borne by a US permanent establishment of that employer.

q: As a nonresident alien with no tax withheld from my income, when is my first 2026 estimated tax payment due?
How much is the failure-to-file penalty per month if my return is late, and what's the cap?
answer: Usually 5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of a month the return is late, but not more than 25%.

q: Can a nonresident alien claim the standard deduction on their tax return?
answer: No, nonresident aliens cannot claim the standard deduction, except certain nonresident aliens from India who are students or business apprentices under Article 21(2) of the U.S.-India treaty.

q: How long can a Danish student or business trainee in the U.S. keep the tax exemption on money from abroad for their training if they're an apprentice?
answer: Apprentices and business trainees can get the exemption for a maximum of 3 years.

q: If a Ukrainian employee works in the U.S. for a foreign employer, what's the maximum number of days they can be in the country and still have their pay exempt from U.S. tax under the treaty?
answer: 183 days during the tax year.

q: What do I do with the A-Number box on the I-765 if I've never had one?
answer: Leave it blank. You only have an A-Number if you were previously in an immigration status like H-1B or H-4, or had OPT authorized before.

q: Where do I find my SEVIS ID number for the I-765 form?
answer: On the top left corner of your I-20.

q: How long can I be unemployed during STEM OPT before I violate my status?
answer: A total of 150 days: 90 days of OPT unemployment plus 60 additional days allowed for STEM OPT.

q: How soon after I get my new I-20 do I have to send in the I-765 to USCIS?
answer: Within 30 days of the I-20 being issued.

q: If I'm on OPT and want to travel abroad while my application is still pending, is that okay?
answer: Traveling outside the U.S. while a POST-completion OPT application is pending is not recommended and can adversely affect reentry; a job offer is required to travel once OPT is approved.

q: Can I count a summer session at UConn toward the one full academic year I need before applying for OPT?
answer: No. Summer term at UConn does not count toward the academic year requirement; only Fall and Spring semesters count.

q: How much do I need to pay USCIS for my OPT application, and how should I pay it?
answer: The UConn guide says $380 by personal check or money order payable to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security; the USCIS I-765 instructions point to the Form G-1055 fee schedule for the current fee.

q: If I'm still working on my thesis and I apply for post-completion OPT, what happens if I don't finish my degree requirements by the OPT end date?
answer: You must complete all degree requirements by your post-completion OPT end date; there is no option to extend your F-1 status if you don't.

q: My name is spelled wrong on the receipt notice I got from USCIS. What should I do?
answer: Contact a DSO/International Advisor at ISSS immediately.

q: If my mail goes to someone else's house, what do I write on the mailing address part of the I-765?
answer: Include an "In Care Of Name" as part of your mailing address, naming the person who receives your mail.

q: How far before my program ends can I file Form I-765 for post-completion OPT, and is there a deadline after the program?
answer: You can file up to 90 days before your program end date, but no later than 60 days after it.

q: I'm a K-1 fiancé(e) on a visa. How long can I work in the U.S. under this category, and can I renew the EAD?
answer: You can only work during your 90 days in K-1 or K-2 status, and you cannot renew this EAD.
